instruction:
Use the Missouri Department of Conservation's Northern Cardinal field guide. Report the scientific name, family and order, the stated length and its measurement endpoints, and the bird's distribution within Missouri. Explain what the page says about migration and possible local movement during unfavorable conditions. Use the written Scientific Name, Size and Where to Find sections, retain the published units, and cite the page rather than identifying features from photographs.

Stopping condition: Stop when the taxonomy, labelled length and Missouri distribution/movement facts are supported by the written field-guide sections.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.description: Evaluate if the agent correctly reported the scientific name of the Northern Cardinal based on the written 'Scientific Name' section of the field guide. Full credit for reporting Cardinalis cardinalis, OR if the website is inaccessible/blocked and the agent clearly reports this issue. Partial credit if there are minor typos.

Evaluate if the agent correctly reported the family and order based on the written 'Scientific Name' section. Full credit for identifying the family (Cardinalidae) and order (Passeriformes), OR if the website is inaccessible/blocked and the agent clearly reports this issue. Partial credit for reporting only one of the two.

items.criterion: Report the stated length and measurement endpoints
items.description: Evaluate if the agent correctly reported the length of the Northern Cardinal and how it is measured, retaining the published units. Full credit for stating the length (e.g., 8-3/4 inches) and the endpoints (from the tip of the bill to the tip of the tail) from the 'Size' section, OR if the website is inaccessible/blocked and the agent clearly reports this issue. Partial credit if the length is provided but measurement endpoints are missing or if units are changed.

Evaluate if the agent correctly reported the bird's distribution within Missouri based on the 'Where to Find' section. Full credit for stating it is found statewide, OR if the website is inaccessible/blocked and the agent clearly reports this issue. Partial credit if the answer is vague but generally correct.

Evaluate if the agent accurately explained the migration and local movement behavior of the Northern Cardinal during unfavorable conditions, based on the 'Where to Find' section. Full credit for stating that they do not migrate but might move locally if conditions are too unfavorable, OR if the website is inaccessible/blocked and the agent clearly reports this issue. Partial credit if only part of the explanation is provided (e.g., mentions non-migratory but omits local movement).

items.criterion: Cite the page and adhere to constraints
items.description: Evaluate if the agent cited the Missouri Department of Conservation page for the information and relied on the written sections (Scientific Name, Size, Where to Find) rather than identifying features from photographs. Full credit if the field-guide source URL is cited and constraints are followed, OR if the website is inaccessible/blocked and the agent clearly reports this issue.
